newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says expects $200 mln for Luz del Sur shares.
newsitem.headline: Peru says expects $200 mln for Luz del Sur shares.

text.p: Peruvian privatization officials estimate the sale of its shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur will raise a total of $200 million, state newspaper El Peruano said Wednesday.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston, chosen Tuesday by the government to handle the international portion of the sale, said the international placement would raise about $100 million.

The remaining revenue would come from the domestic sale, which will be directed by local bank Banco Continental , according to Javier Tovar, head of the Luz del Sur privatization committee, El Peruano reported.
The government holds a 30 percent stake in the electricity company, but has not formally specified what portion of its shares it will sell.
The sale will go ahead before the end of the year in three separate tranches, according to Tovar.

In the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals under the Citizens' Participation in Privatization scheme, Banco Continental will direct a group of local banks that includes Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru -- Santander SAB -- will direct a group of local brokerages to book-build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.
CS First Boston beat out bids Tuesday from investment banks Kleinwort Benson, J.P. Morgan and Merrill Lynch to win the right to handle the international placement.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
In July, J.P. Morgan and Merrill Lynch handled the international placement of a $1.25 billion sale of a 26.6 percent state-held stake in Telefonica del Peru .
